text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- All newspapers reported on bomb attacks in capital Tirana which left 27 people injured on Monday.
- Italian ambassador Paolo Foresti, recently accused by Albanian newspapers of bias in favour of President Sali Berisha, will stay in post until elections set for June 29.
- The Central Election Commission decided that Albanian voters will use stamps instead of personal signatures to prevent fraud attempts.
- Six masked gunmen plundered a bus in the southern town of Skrapar. One of President Sali Berisha's economics advisers was among the robbed passengers.

- Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi assured President Sali Berisha that Italy would contribute in monitoring upcoming parliamentary elections, saying the strength of a multinational force to guard polling stations would increase.
- The refusal of Prime Minister Bashkim Fino to attend the lunch President Sali Berisha offered in honour of Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi showed Berisha-Fino relations have worsened.
- King Leka, seeking support for the restoration of the monarchy, had a lukewarm visit in the southernmost town of Gjirokaster.
- Seven people were killed in Erseke town when a woman and her boyfriend fired with Kalashnikovs at customers in a snack bar.
- Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi urged Albanian authorities to disband the so-called committees of public salvation ahead of elections.
- State-run television has favoured the Socialist Party's electoral campaign, a survey by the Institute for Democratic Culture shows.
- We will never make coaltions with leftist parties which incited communist rebellion, Democratic Party leaders say.
- The Socialist Party will rebuild what Berisha's dictatorship destroyed over the last five years, leader Fatos Nano told an enthusiastic crowed in the southeastern town of Korce.
- Tens of cars with gunmen accompany Berisha when he goes out of Tirana to hold rallies for his Democratic Party, the paper says.
